project.name: QuickJS
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected here is the ARVO workspace checkout at `2788d71e823b522b178db3b3660ce93689534e6d`. That checkout is newer than the metadata's vulnerable commit, but the specific vulnerable lines used here in `quickjs.c` (`__JS_EvalInternal`, `js_evaluate_module`, `JS_CallInternal`, `JS_ThrowError2`, `build_backtrace`, and `find_line_num`) match the metadata-era vulnerable code shown by `git show 9b587c4:quickjs.c`.

classification.classification_note: ARVO metadata labels this sample `unclassified`, but the saved Stage 01 witness proves a concrete uninitialized read: module evaluation executes the compiled module through the normal synchronous `JS_CallFree` / `JS_CallInternal` path, which leaves the active `JSStackFrame.cur_pc` indeterminate when interrupt-driven error reporting builds a backtrace and calls `find_line_num()`.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the implementation of module linking and evaluation due to lack of proper top-level-await support, which does not follow the specification and can result in errors when handling cycling module dependencies.
bug_description.original_source: CyberGym tasks.json / staged vulnerable source / staged patch.diff / Stage 01 reproduction artifacts
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 13-byte file `poc`, whose 12-byte module source is ASCII `for(;;)/ /-2` followed by a terminating NUL. QuickJS parses that text in module mode and materializes module bytecode whose loop body repeatedly evaluates a RegExp object minus integer `2`; the saved crash stack confirms execution reaches `js_binary_arith_slow()` and RegExp coercion while running under `js_evaluate_module()`. In the vulnerable source, `js_evaluate_module()` executes `m->func_obj` through the normal synchronous `JS_CallFree()` path. That path enters `JS_CallInternal()`, allocates stack-local frame `JSStackFrame sf_s`, and later installs it as `rt->current_stack_frame` before any store to `sf->cur_pc`. When the loop has polled enough times, a nested runtime call in the RegExp-to-number coercion path raises `interrupted`; `JS_ThrowError2()` immediately builds a backtrace, and `build_backtrace()` passes `sf->cur_pc - b->byte_code_buf - 1` to `find_line_num()`. Because `sf->cur_pc` was never initialized on this synchronous module path, MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `quickjs.c:6437` in `find_line_num()`. The staged patch replaces synchronous module execution with promise/async module evaluation and spec-compliant module status tracking for top-level-await/cycle handling; that new path routes modules through `js_async_function_call()`, whose `async_func_init()` initializes `sf->cur_pc = b->byte_code_buf` before execution begins.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the attacker-controlled module text. This call loads the exact witness bytes into QuickJS parse state so the source string can be compiled into the module function later executed on the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 13 bytes: ASCII `for(;;)/ /-2` plus a trailing NUL (`sha256 9692afeb29728fd9ecf9cba75c4b2d81b59c67d2ee1a7292cc6d8cf840b23211`). The harness calls `JS_Eval(..., Size - 1, ..., JS_EVAL_FLAG_COMPILE_ONLY | JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL | JS_EVAL_TYPE_MODULE)`, so `input_len` here is the 12-byte source text without the terminator.
source.note: Scored source step. The harness boundary `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` is intentionally not used as the source.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The uninitialized value later reported by MemorySanitizer is `sf_s.cur_pc` from this stack-local frame. On the normal bytecode-call path, `cur_pc` is not initialized at declaration time and remains indeterminate when the frame is made current.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved MSan trace names the allocation of `sf_s` in `JS_CallInternal` as the origin. The concrete field consumed at the sink is `sf->cur_pc`, which is first created by this declaration and only written later on selected call/exception paths.

root_cause.description: Missing module-evaluation obligation. The vulnerable module evaluator runs the module body through the normal synchronous `JS_CallFree` / `JS_CallInternal` path instead of the promise/async module path introduced by the fix, so later error reporting can observe a current stack frame whose `cur_pc` has never been initialized.
root_cause.note: The staged patch removes this synchronous module-call path in favor of async/promise-driven module evaluation (`fd->func_kind = JS_FUNC_ASYNC`, `js_execute_sync_module()`, and `js_async_function_call()`).

sink.description: MemorySanitizer sink. `find_line_num()` compares the uninitialized `pc_value` derived from `sf->cur_pc` while mapping the backtrace line number for the interrupt error.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `quickjs.c:6437:13` in `find_line_num`.

parser_admitted.description: Parsing has succeeded and QuickJS materializes executable code from the exact witness instead of returning a syntax error, so the source text is admitted onto the later module-evaluation path.

module_eval_gate.description: Once the compile-only path wraps the parsed source as `JS_TAG_MODULE`, `JS_EvalFunctionInternal()` takes the module-specific evaluator path rather than the ordinary function path.

evidence_limitations: The staged checkout is a later QuickJS snapshot (`2788d71e823b522b178db3b3660ce93689534e6d`), not the metadata's vulnerable commit. This GT anchors only lines that match the metadata-era vulnerable code exactly.

The staged issue description and patch are about top-level-await and cycling-module semantics, but the saved Stage 01 witness is a one-module source string with no literal `await` or import cycle. This GT therefore uses the patch only to explain the module-evaluation path change that removes the witnessed MSan symptom.

Stage 02 did not rerun a fixed build, and `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation. The claim that the staged patch resolves this particular MSan symptom is source-grounded inference from the new async module path (`js_async_function_call()` plus `async_func_init()` setting `sf->cur_pc`), not direct fixed-version runtime evidence.

fine_trace.note: Source. QuickJS first consumes the attacker-controlled module text here and stores it in parse state. For the saved witness, this is the 12-byte source string `for(;;)/ /-2`, which the harness evaluates in module mode.

The admitted source text is materialized as executable module state. On the saved witness, the resulting module bytecode repeatedly reaches `js_binary_arith_slow()` on a RegExp object while running the loop body implied by `for(;;)/ /-2`, as shown by the saved crash stack's `js_evaluate_module -> JS_CallInternal -> js_binary_arith_slow` frames.

fine_trace.code:
ret_val = JS_CallFree(ctx, m->func_obj, JS_UNDEFINED, 0, NULL);
m->func_obj = JS_UNDEFINED;
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The vulnerable module evaluator executes the module body through the normal synchronous bytecode-call path. The staged patch replaces this with promise/async module execution, which is the semantic change that removes the later uninitialized-frame state.

Uninitialized-value origin. The synchronous module-call path allocates a stack-local `JSStackFrame`, and its `cur_pc` field starts indeterminate here. MemorySanitizer traces the poisoned value back to this frame allocation.

The outer module frame becomes the runtime's current stack frame before any store to `sf->cur_pc`. From this point until a later explicit `sf->cur_pc = ...` write, any backtrace walk that consults the current frame will observe an uninitialized program counter.

While the outer module frame from step 5 is still current and `sf->cur_pc` is still unset, the witness's loop body coerces a RegExp object to a number. The saved stack shows this path descending through `JS_ToPrimitiveFree`, `js_regexp_toString`, and nested `JS_CallInternal()` / property access before the interrupt error is raised.

After the nested interrupt path raises `interrupted`, the error-construction path immediately requests a backtrace. The saved crash stack shows `__js_poll_interrupts -> JS_ThrowInternalError -> JS_ThrowError -> JS_ThrowError2 -> build_backtrace` on the witnessed run.

Backtrace construction consumes the current outer module frame and computes `pc_value` from `sf->cur_pc`. Because step 5 never initialized that field before the interrupt error reached here, this call propagates the uninitialized program counter directly into `find_line_num()`.
Sink. `find_line_num()` compares the uninitialized `pc_value` derived in step 8. This is the exact `use-of-uninitialized-value` site reported by the saved MemorySanitizer trace.

allocation_context.note: MSan reports the origin as allocation of `sf_s` in this stack frame; the concrete vulnerable declaration is `JSStackFrame sf_s, *sf = &sf_s;` at line 16206.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: Parsed from staged `default_crash_trace.txt` / `sanitizer_trace.txt`; cross-checked against the exact staged QuickJS checkout and the staged `patch.diff`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved MemorySanitizer trace reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `quickjs.c:6437:13` in `find_line_num`, which is the exact sink anchored above.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSan attributes the poisoned value to stack allocation `sf_s` in `JS_CallInternal`; the fine trace's tainted-value origin is that `JSStackFrame` declaration, and the root-cause step is the preceding `js_evaluate_module()` decision to execute modules on that synchronous path.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack aligns with the fine trace as `js_evaluate_module` (frame 27) -> outer `JS_CallInternal` / `js_binary_arith_slow` (frames 25 and 24) -> nested RegExp coercion / interrupt path (frames 17, 11, 7, 6, 5) -> `JS_ThrowError2` / `build_backtrace` / `find_line_num` (frames 2, 1, 0).
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 5 installs `sf_s` as `rt->current_stack_frame` before any store to `sf->cur_pc`; step 8 then passes `sf->cur_pc - b->byte_code_buf - 1` into `find_line_num()`, whose `pc_value` parameter is consumed at the reported sink.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch removes synchronous `ret_val = JS_CallFree(ctx, m->func_obj, JS_UNDEFINED, 0, NULL);` module execution and replaces it with promise/async module evaluation (`js_execute_sync_module()` / `js_async_function_call()`). That async path uses `async_func_init()`, which explicitly sets `sf->cur_pc = b->byte_code_buf` before execution, so the specific uninitialized current-frame program counter consumed at the sink no longer exists on the patched module path.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's authoritative runtime evidence is `default_crash_trace.txt` / `sanitizer_trace.txt`, captured from stock vulnerable image `n132/arvo:46957-vul`, which show `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `find_line_num()` while evaluating the exact module source from `poc`. On the witnessed run, that source is compiled as a module, repeatedly executes the loop body implied by `for(;;)/ /-2`, and eventually raises an interrupt error during RegExp numeric coercion while the outer module frame still has uninitialized `cur_pc` state.

format.name: QuickJS module source text
format.contract: The only verified trigger is the exact 13-byte file `gt_results/arvo_46957/poc` (sha256 `9692afeb29728fd9ecf9cba75c4b2d81b59c67d2ee1a7292cc6d8cf840b23211`), which `fuzz_compile` consumes as 12 bytes of module source plus a terminating NUL: ASCII `for(;;)/ /-2`. In the saved run this exact source is admitted as a module, its loop body repeatedly reaches RegExp-to-number coercion, and after enough interrupt polls error reporting consults an outer module frame whose `cur_pc` was never initialized. No broader class of JavaScript modules, loop constructs, or regex-arithmetic expressions is claimed.
